## Judgment

### Expected-drift set

Two commits. `608f0f0` edits only `modules/tools/ssh-tpm-agent.nix`, which
sweet16 and petunia import directly. `bff918c` edits `modules/core/users.nix`
— reached by every NixOS host through both the workstation and server
profiles — plus the `groot` blocks in `hosts/avina/default.nix` and
`hosts/hermes/default.nix`.

Expected: all four NixOS hosts drift. The standalone groot HM configurations
are a different user on non-NixOS hosts and must not move.

This is the first commit in this series where avina and hermes are *expected*
to drift; every previous one had them byte-identical. That is the enrollment
reaching them, not a leak.

### Actual vs expected

Matches. `verify-drift.sh 42a8955 HEAD`: sweet16, petunia, avina and hermes
all drift; groot@dualie and groot@forge byte-identical; groot@rk3588 N/A
(aarch64, not evaluable on this builder).

### Why the keys carry no PIN

Two measured facts, not a preference:

- The agent is a daemon with no tty, so a PIN must come from an askpass.
  ssh-tpm-agent only probes FHS paths (`/usr/lib/ssh/gnome-ssh-askpass`,
  `/usr/bin/ksshaskpass`, ...) that do not exist on NixOS, and it logs
  "system does not have an askpass program" and refuses every signature.
  These hosts are driven headless, so a GUI prompt could not be answered
  regardless.
- Caching requires the kernel keyctl helpers. `/sbin/request-key` is absent
  and the agent logs "kernel is missing the keyctl executable helpers",
  caching nothing. A PIN would therefore have been demanded on *every*
  signature rather than once per agent lifetime — which was the premise the
  PIN decision rested on. Against petunia's 3-attempt lockout that would have
  been actively hazardous.

A `systemd-ask-password --user` wrapper was built and tested rather than
assumed. It works, but needs a tmpfiles rule to chown
`/run/user/%U/systemd/ask-password` plus a bespoke answering script, because
`systemd-tty-ask-password-agent` handles only *system* requests and has no
`--user` option. Rejected as disproportionate. Test state was reverted.

### Why P-256 and not P-384

`ssh-tpm-keygen --supported` reports `ecdsa bit lengths: 256 384` on both
hosts, but that advertises key *creation*, not signing. On petunia, P-384
signing fails with `TPM_RC_SIZE (parameter 1): structure is the wrong size`
while P-256 returns rc=0. sweet16 handles both. A single curve fleet-wide
beats per-host divergence.

### Verified end to end

Both hosts now sign through the real socket-activated units, not a hand-run
agent:

  petunia  personal rc=0   agentic rc=0
  sweet16  personal rc=0   agentic rc=0

sweet16 required a restart before this worked: its systemd user manager
started 2026-08-07, predating `nix-nexus.tpm2.users`, and children inherit the
manager's supplementary groups — so the units failed with
`open /dev/tpmrm0: permission denied` while a fresh ssh login succeeded. The
manager now carries gid 982. petunia was resolved the same way via
`loginctl terminate-user`.

The enrolled sweet16 blob was compared against the on-disk public key after
the reboot and matches, confirming TPM-sealed keys survive a power cycle.

### Not yet done

The ed25519 key remains in every `authorized_keys` list and `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`
still points at gpg-agent, so nothing depends on the TPM path yet. The agentic
keys are not registered with GitHub or Gitea, and `ForwardAgent` in
`~/.ssh/config.d/13-permafrost.conf` is still commented out.
